Adjudicating between the two explanations is a design problem rather than an interpretive one. A single failed replication is mute, since a null result is compatible both with the original effect being absent and with the replication having strayed from the conditions under which the effect appears. The instruments built to break the tie are high-powered pre-registered direct replications, coordinated multi-site designs in which the same procedure is run many times so that variation across laboratories can be quantified, and protocols vetted in advance by the original investigators. [1]

Of those replications, 36 produced statistically significant effects in the original direction, which shows that fewer than half of the Reproducibility Project: Psychology replications reached statistical significance. Either that minority tally stands, or at least half of the Reproducibility Project: Psychology replications reached statistical significance; one of the two must be the case, and they cannot both be. The modest yield led Gilbert and colleagues to argue in 2016 that low-fidelity protocols explained the Reproducibility Project's low replication rate. Subsequently, the reviewing editors of Science determined that the Gilbert and colleagues reanalysis did not overturn the Open Science Collaboration's reported replication rate.

Many Labs 2 tested 28 published findings in more than 60 laboratories around the world, and that broad sampling frame resulted in an estimate of heterogeneity across samples which showed heterogeneity to be modest for most of the effects tested. Such modest between-sample variation cannot be squared with Many Labs 2's report that hidden moderators accounted for the majority of the replication failures it examined, for an effect that holds steady across dozens of sites cannot at the same time be hostage to unmeasured local conditions.

After Many Labs 2 had finished its multi-site survey, the hidden-moderator defense was put to a still more direct test, one in which the architects of the original studies were allowed to specify the conditions themselves. Many Labs 5 revised replication protocols with input from the original authors and from peer reviewers, and that revision yielded effect sizes no larger than those obtained from the earlier replication protocols. The parity of those effect sizes cannot be squared with Many Labs 5's demonstration that expert-revised protocols raised replication success to the rate observed in the original publications, since a revision cannot both leave the measured effects exactly where they stood and lift success to the level of the original reports.

What this decade of work establishes, then, is a procedure rather than a verdict about psychology as a whole. Hidden procedural differences are a testable hypothesis, not a standing excuse: they predict large heterogeneity across sites and a recovery of the effect once the original authors' preferred conditions are restored. Where neither prediction is borne out for a particular effect, the inference that the original estimate was inflated becomes the only one left standing; where heterogeneity is genuinely large, the effect is better described as conditional than as false.

Adjudicating between genuine generalization and contamination of the training data is a matter of designing evaluations whose outcomes come apart under the two hypotheses. The first family of methods is behavioural. Researchers construct a fresh test set whose items were written after the model's training cutoff date. Scale AI's release of GSM1k as a held-out benchmark reconstructing the distribution of GSM8K shows that such post-cutoff construction can indeed be carried out at scale and at matched difficulty. Model accuracy on GSM-Symbolic declines as the number of clauses in a problem increases. Perturbing surface features such as proper names and numeric values tests a model's robustness to superficial changes. After that release of GSM1k, the model's accuracy fell by 13 percentage points on the newly authored problems, a gap of the size one expects when familiar items have been seen rather than solved. By contrast, the headline result of the GSM1k study was that GPT-4 suffered the largest accuracy drop among all evaluated models, which shifts the interpretive burden onto the strongest systems rather than the weakest.

The second family of methods works on the data and the model itself rather than on aggregate scores, and its value depends on what an external auditor is actually permitted to examine. n-gram overlap analysis compares benchmark strings against the text of the pretraining corpus. Closed-weight models prevent direct inspection of their training corpora by outside researchers.

A contaminated model can reproduce verbatim continuations of benchmark items when prompted with their prefixes, which shows that membership inference attacks estimate whether a specific example was present in a model's training data. The impossibility of auditing a sealed corpus from the outside has therefore led directly to statistics computed from the model alone: Min-K% Prob scores a sequence using the probabilities of its least likely tokens. That corpus requirement cannot be squared with a quantity read off the lowest-probability tokens of the candidate sequence, and the practice of membership inference described above rules it out as well, since estimating whether a particular example was seen is undertaken precisely where the corpus cannot be consulted at all. Converging verdicts from post-cutoff retesting, variant generation and model-side detection are what finally settle the question for any given system.

Adjudicating between drug-induced liver injury and an underlying viral or autoimmune hepatitis turns on biochemistry, timing, and the systematic exclusion of competing causes. The patient developed jaundice three weeks after starting amoxicillin-clavulanate. [1] That the injury is hepatocellular in pattern is evidence that the jaundice arose from direct injury to hepatocytes. At least one of two mechanisms is at work in a presentation of this kind — direct damage to hepatocytes or impaired bile flow within the liver — and perhaps both.

Serology then narrows the field. After the aminotransferase elevation was documented, clinicians tested for hepatitis A IgM, hepatitis B surface antigen, and hepatitis C RNA. A positive hepatitis C IgG antibody result confirms acute hepatitis C infection. Hepatitis E serology, by contrast with that three-virus panel, is recommended in the workup of suspected drug-induced liver injury.

The autoimmune limb of the differential is the more treacherous one. Antinuclear antibody and anti-smooth muscle antibody positivity supports a diagnosis of autoimmune hepatitis; such reactivity indicated to a consulting hepatologist that the process was autoimmune, and he attributed the liver injury to underlying autoimmune hepatitis. A normal antinuclear antibody titre excludes autoimmune hepatitis; that exclusionary rule and the diagnostic weight carried by antinuclear and anti-smooth muscle antibody positivity cannot both be true, and the reliance placed on such reactivity rules the former out.

The treating physician attributed the jaundice to the newly started antibiotic, an attribution that cannot be squared with the hepatologist's assignment of the injury to underlying autoimmune disease, since one agent or the other, but not both accounts, can be the cause. Spatial pattern is the first thing a field diagnostician reads in a declining crop. Pathogen-caused decline typically appears in discrete patches that expand along planting rows over successive weeks, whereas nutrient deficiency symptoms appear uniformly across soil zones of similar texture and topography. Nutrient deficiencies spread from plant to plant through contact with soil water, a mode of transmission that cannot be reconciled with an even expression of symptoms wherever soil texture and topography are alike.

Diagnosticians split the taproot and lower stem of affected plants to examine the vascular tissue for discoloration. [1] Foliar morphology is read alongside such internal inspection: potassium deficiency in soybean produces chlorosis and necrosis along the margins of upper leaves, and potassium deficiency produces dark necrotic fungal lesions on the soybean taproot, a root pathology that cannot be squared with a mineral disorder whose expression is confined to marginal scorch of the leaf. Laboratory support is assembled in parallel with the field examination. The soil test reported exchangeable potassium levels for the affected area of the field. Sectioning of the taproots and lower stems showed that Fusarium virguliforme was present in the root tissue of the declining plants, and the reported exchangeable values indicated that soil potassium in the affected area was below the critical level for soybean. At least one of those two conditions obtained in that part of the field, fungal colonization of the roots or a sub-critical potassium supply, and perhaps both obtained together.

Culture work on the symptomatic tissue yields a result that admits no middle ground. Either no plant pathogen was isolated from the symptomatic root tissue, or at least one plant pathogen was isolated from it; one of the two outcomes must be the case, and the two cannot hold together. Which outcome the plates deliver determines whether the investigation proceeds to inoculation work or turns instead to the fertility program and the soil chemistry of the site.

A ruling of this kind carries weight because it rests on an agent that was both recovered and shown to reproduce the disorder in healthy plants.

Attribution in a contested breach begins with the authentication record itself, because the question of who signed on, from where, and by what mechanism is settled by machine-generated artifacts rather than by the parties' competing narratives. Because Windows Event ID 4624 records successful logon events on the affected systems, the logon type carried in those authentication events confirms that the session was a remote interactive connection. Windows Event ID 4625 records successful logons to a domain-joined host, and that coding cannot both be true alongside the assignment of successful logon recording to Event ID 4624; the two mappings rule each other out, so the examiner must determine which identifier the logs actually carry before any conclusion about remote access is drawn.

VPN concentrator logs showed the administrator account authenticating from an IP address allocated to a foreign hosting provider, which confirms the remote interactive character attributed to the session in the logon-type field. The same concentrator data also establishes the geographic finding: impossible-travel analysis flagged two successful logons to the same account from locations 6,000 kilometres apart within eleven minutes, a separation no traveller could cross in that interval.

Investigators recovered USB device connection artifacts from the Windows registry of the employee's workstation. NetFlow records captured a single outbound transfer of 40 gigabytes from the database server. Badge records placed the administrator off the premises at the time of the 40-gigabyte transfer; that is, the administrator was not physically present in the building when the data was copied out. [1] That absence from the site stands in contrast with the USB device connection artifacts recovered from the workstation registry, which point instead to hands-on activity at the machine.

The victim organization asserted that the vendor's managed detection service failed to alert on the bulk outbound transfer. The security vendor asserted that a departing database administrator deliberately removed the data. The administrator's absence from the building when the data left and the attribution of the removal to that departing administrator cannot both be true; the physical-access record rules out the vendor's version of events. What remains for the examiner is to show, from timeline reconstruction, which account was used and whether its use is consistent with a credentialed outsider operating over the concentrator.

The managed services contract obliged the vendor to monitor endpoint telemetry 24 hours a day. The intrusion went undetected for 18 days after the first unauthorized logon. Whereas the eighteen days of unobserved intrusion govern the allocation of contractual responsibility between the parties, the GDPR requires a controller to notify the supervisory authority within 30 days of becoming aware of a personal data breach, a period measured from awareness rather than from the moment of compromise. Disciplined forensic practice therefore settles the insider-versus-intruder question on artifact convergence, leaving the contractual and regulatory consequences to follow from the timeline so established.

Investigators fix the temporal and spatial boundaries of the event, characterise the exposures the animals shared, and then ask which candidate cause predicts the observed pattern of who died, where, and how quickly. Each candidate is treated as a hypothesis with determinate consequences for gross pathology, microbiology and toxicology, and the hypothesis whose consequences fail is discarded.

The 2015 event in Kazakhstan remains the standard worked example. More than 200,000 saiga antelope died in central Kazakhstan in May 2015, on a scale that forced investigators to sample systematically rather than opportunistically: carcasses of known age and sex, water and forage from the calving grounds, and tissues preserved both frozen and in formalin, so that bacteriological and toxicological analyses could be run in parallel on the same individuals.

Each affected saiga herd died within a span of a few days. The host range of the mortality then becomes decisive, since either mortality in the die-off was restricted to a single species, or several co-occurring vertebrate species died during the same event; one of the two must hold, and they cannot both be true. Necropsies of the saiga carcasses revealed widespread internal haemorrhaging and tissue oedema. Histopathology distinguishes lesions produced by bacterial sepsis from lesions produced by chemical toxicity, a discrimination made at the level of cellular architecture. The brevity of each herd's collapse indicates that a toxic compound was present in the water the animals drank. The haemorrhage and oedema recorded at necropsy indicate that an infectious agent was circulating in the affected population, and at least one of the two — a toxic compound in the drinking water or a circulating infectious agent — was in play, perhaps both. Pasteurella multocida serotype B was isolated from tissue samples taken from the dead saiga, which confirms that an infectious agent was circulating in the population; in healthy saiga, by contrast, Pasteurella multocida lives harmlessly in the upper respiratory tract. Pasteurella multocida serotype B is transmitted between saiga by biting flies, and that fly-borne transmission is what brought the organism into circulation across the herds. Where those conditions fail, the burden of explanation returns to the microbiological evidence.

A plaintiff must prove causation beyond a reasonable doubt in a negligence action. Any intervening act by a third party automatically relieves the original defendant of liability; that proposition cannot be reconciled with the principle that a foreseeable intervening cause leaves the chain of proximate causation intact, and a court cannot apply the two together. Courts accordingly disentangle the competing strands by asking whether the supervening event fell within the range of hazards that the defendant's carelessness created, and by scrutinising the quality of the proof offered on each side of that question. Expert testimony is commonly used to establish medical causation in personal injury cases, and that reliance led to the Daubert standard, which governs the admissibility of expert causation testimony in federal court.

The controversy over the Reichstag fire shows in miniature how historians weigh rival reconstructions of an event whose documentary trail is broken and partisan. The Reichstag building in Berlin was set on fire on the night of 27 February 1933. Within a day the Nazi government publicly attributed the fire to a communist insurrectionary conspiracy, and that attribution led directly to the Reichstag Fire Decree of 28 February 1933, which suspended most civil liberties guaranteed by the Weimar constitution. [1]

Nearly three decades after the fire, in 1962, Fritz Tobias published his book-length study of it. Tobias held a chair in modern history at the University of Göttingen. Tobias argued that van der Lubbe was the sole perpetrator of the arson; that is, his thesis was that no person other than van der Lubbe set the Reichstag alight. Set against that 1962 study, by contrast, was the work of Walther Hofer, who convened an international committee of historians that argued for Nazi complicity in the fire. Van der Lubbe had accomplices in setting the Reichstag fire, a finding that cannot be squared with the contention that nobody but he put a torch to the building.

Adjudication between such accounts is not a matter of preferring the more dramatic story, nor of counting heads among specialists. Historians apply source criticism to test the authenticity, provenance and internal consistency of documents. They treat testimony recorded decades after an event as weaker evidence than contemporaneous records, since recollection decays and late statements are shaped by the very controversies they enter.

A sworn 1955 statement by the SA member Hans-Martin Lennings came to light in 2019 in the records of the Hanover public prosecutor's office. Moral realism holds that moral judgments describe objective moral facts; expressivism, by contrast, holds that moral judgments express the speaker's non-cognitive attitudes. Shorn of its technical apparatus, the realist thesis is simply that moral judgments report facts about the world, and the terms of the disagreement ensure that at least one of that thesis and the competing claim that moral judgments express the attitudes of the speaker who utters them must be correct, perhaps both together. Most of the pressure on the expressivist side arises from its semantic commitments. Since expressivism construes a moral verdict as the voicing of an attitude rather than the description of a state of affairs, it issues in non-cognitivism, which denies that moral sentences are truth-apt; in other words, on non-cognitivism moral utterances are incapable of being either true or false. That very incapacity generated the best-known objection to the programme. The Frege-Geach problem presses expressivists to explain the behaviour of moral terms embedded in conditionals, and that pressure led Simon Blackburn to develop quasi-realism to account for the apparently factual surface of moral discourse.

Adjudicating a disputed affiliation turns less on how many words two languages share than on what kind of patterning those words exhibit. Regular sound correspondences between two languages are the standard evidence for genetic relationship. The comparative method requires reconstruction of a proto-language from the attested daughter languages. Mass lexical comparison without reconstruction is rejected by most historical linguists. [1] A procedure that predicts the phonological shape of each cognate form, rather than one that tabulates resemblances, is what makes inheritance and borrowing distinguishable in the first place.

Within that framework the available evidence is ranked. Shared irregular morphology is treated as among the strongest evidence of common descent, since suppletive paradigms and arbitrary allomorphy are not transferred wholesale across a contact boundary. By contrast, shared basic word order is accepted by historical linguists as proof of genetic relationship. Typological traits such as tone and monosyllabicity can spread between unrelated neighbouring languages, and that diffusibility cannot be squared with granting shared basic word order the status of proof of common descent.

Loanwords cluster in semantic fields tied to trade, religion, and technology, and that distribution confirms that shared basic vocabulary such as body-part and kinship terms is relatively resistant to borrowing. Numerals form a contrast to that merely relative resistance: they are never borrowed between languages in contact. Correspondences concentrated in the resistant core of the lexicon therefore carry a weight that parallels in cultural vocabulary do not.

The history of Vietnamese shows how such a dispute is resolved in practice. Henri Maspero classified Vietnamese as a Tai language in 1912, pointing to its tonal system, its monosyllabic word shapes and a sizeable stock of words shared with Tai. [2] At least one of two ordinary explanations covers that shared stock, and perhaps both do: some of the lexical resemblances between Vietnamese and Tai languages are the product of borrowing, these being the very similarities that led Maspero to his classification, and some of the lexical resemblances between Vietnamese and Tai languages are the product of accidental similarity. Once the borrowed layer is set aside, regular correspondences in body-part terms, kinship terms and verbal morphology align Vietnamese with Mon-Khmer, and the borrowed character of the Tai parallels indicates that Vietnamese is a member of the Austroasiatic family. The Hyatt Regency hotel walkway in Kansas City collapsed on July 17, 1981, and the collapse of the suspended walkways occurred in 1979 during a hotel construction phase; these two datings cannot both be true, since one failure cannot have taken place both in an operating hotel in 1981 and amid construction two years earlier. The wreckage is interrogated first. Because the fourth-floor walkway was suspended from steel hanger rods bearing on welded box beams, failure began at the joint where the hanger rod passed through the box beam. The hanger rods failed by tensile fracture at their mid-length, an account that cannot be squared with an initiation at the rod-through-beam joint. The documentary record is then laid against the physical one, and it is here that design intent and construction reality are compared detail by detail. That is why macroeconomists treat the joint path of prices and quantities, both at the onset of an inflation and through its retreat, as the decisive body of evidence.

The dispute is then organized by a taxonomy and a governing principle. Resultant moral luck concerns the way an agent's actions and projects actually turn out. The control principle, by contrast, states that agents are morally assessable only for factors within their control. Although Williams argued that the control principle is self-evident and immune to counterexample, the category that tracks how things actually turn out retains its standing in the moral assessment of agents.

Two standards of wrongness divide the field. Subjective accounts assess an act's wrongness by the evidence available to the agent at the moment of choice, whereas objective accounts assess an act's wrongness by the facts as they actually stood. [1] In legal settings a further standard operates: negligence requires a breach of a duty of reasonable care. Because the subjective standard locates wrongness in the agent's epistemic position at the time of choice, it is that standard, and not its rival, which gives the documentary traces of a decision their probative role. Hindsight bias leads evaluators to overestimate how predictable an outcome was, and it is for that reason that contemporaneous records of a deliberation serve as evidence of the reasons available to the agent at the time.

Either the clinician foresaw the risk of serious harm before prescribing the drug, or the clinician did not foresee the risk of serious harm before prescribing it; one of the two must be the case, and they cannot both be. Attributing a system-wide blackout either to the variability of wind and solar output or to the configuration of protection and control equipment is an evidentiary exercise, and it begins with measurement. Investigators reconstruct the event sequence using time-synchronised phasor measurement unit data, and that reconstruction in turn brings about the validation of dynamic simulation models of the power system against the measured responses recorded during the event. Phasor measurement units record one voltage and current reading per minute. Put differently, the reconstruction of the sequence is largely an exercise in supervisory control and data acquisition records, since SCADA systems log time-stamped circuit breaker and relay operations used to order the event sequence. [1]

That validation work is necessarily undertaken after the physical events it is built to reproduce. Tornado-strength winds damaged transmission towers in South Australia on 28 September 2016. Federal ministers publicly attributed the South Australian blackout to the state's high share of wind generation. Once the towers had been brought down, one of two accounts must hold: either South Australia separated from the rest of the National Electricity Market during the 28 September 2016 disturbance, or it remained synchronously connected to the rest of the market throughout that disturbance; one of the two is the case, and not both.

The recorded data for that evening show that the blackout occurred during a period of zero wind output across the entire state. The Heywood interconnector tripped after the sudden reduction in South Australian wind farm output, and that trip cannot be squared with a state-wide absence of wind generation at the moment of collapse, since the two cannot both be true of the same minutes. The same state-wide absence of output indicates that the ministerial attribution of the blackout to the state's high share of wind generation was well founded.

Beyond the sequence itself, two bodies of record are assembled before any cause is assigned. Investigators compare recorded wind farm output with the pre-dispatch forecast output for the minutes before the disturbance. Protection relay setting records and control firmware versions are obtained by investigators from the turbine manufacturers. By contrast with the question of how much energy the farms actually delivered against expectation, the settings inquiry asks whether plant was configured to stay on line at all. Voltage ride-through settings determine whether a generating unit remains connected during a network fault. Another part of the settings file concerns rate-of-change-of-frequency relays, which can disconnect generation during fast frequency excursions.

Only when the measured sequence, the deviation from forecast and the as-configured protection and control parameters are laid side by side does the attribution question become answerable. A resource-driven explanation requires generation to have fallen away before any protection acted, while a settings-driven explanation requires units to have been taken off line by their own configured thresholds while fuel, wind or sunlight remained available.

Adjudication begins by acknowledging that texts and strata answer different questions: a scribe records what mattered to a court, whereas a destruction horizon records only that a building burned. Radiocarbon dating of destruction layers supplies a chronology independent of the textual record, and it shows that the Late Bronze Age collapse unfolded across the eastern Mediterranean between roughly 1200 and 1150 BCE. By contrast, dendrochronological sequences fix the onset of the collapse precisely to the year 1177 BCE. That precision cannot be squared with the documentary history of the figure, for a chronological review panel ultimately determined that 1177 BCE is a symbolic marker derived from Egyptian records rather than a tree-ring-fixed date.

Within the textual record itself, the first task is to establish who is speaking and when. Inscriptions at Medinet Habu record Ramesses III's battles against a coalition known as the Sea Peoples. The Medinet Habu reliefs date the great naval battle against the Sea Peoples to the eighth year of Merneptah; such an attribution cannot stand together with the fact that it is Ramesses III whose campaigns those same temple walls commemorate. Cuneiform tablets from Ugarit describe hostile ships appearing off the Syrian coast, raiders sighted there before Ramesses III ever joined battle with the coalition, even though the surviving cuneiform archives preserve the perspectives of palace elites rather than rural populations.

Where independent lines of inquiry converge, an account becomes much harder to resist. The Hittite capital Hattusa ceased to function as an imperial centre around 1200 BCE, an outcome brought about by a protracted failure of rainfall across the region, and its abandonment shows that the Hittite empire ceased to exist as a political entity in the early twelfth century BCE; in other words, Hittite imperial rule came to an end during the first decades of the 1100s BCE. The force of the inference lies in the fact that the stratigraphic evidence of abandonment was not curated by anyone with an interest in how the dynasty would be remembered.

The proxies that settle such questions are precisely those no scribe shaped. [1] Adjudication, on this model, is less a verdict for one kind of source against another than a ranking of constraints: chronologies anchored outside the archives fix the sequence of events, the archives explain what contemporaries understood themselves to be facing, and only a narrative that survives both sets of limits earns provisional assent.

Silent data corruption refers to a computation producing an incorrect result with no error reported by the hardware, and that is exactly the category into which the episode falls: the miscomputation was a silent data corruption — in other words, the data was corrupted without any error being signalled by the machine. Against that picture of a failure that announces itself nowhere in the logs stands the protection offered by ECC memory, which corrects double-bit errors within a single DRAM word.

Because the corruption occurred with no signal from the machine, this indicates that the machine contained a defective hardware component. The program contained a latent software defect as well, so at least one of the two faults — a bad part in the machine or a dormant bug in the code — was responsible, and perhaps both were. Adjudication accordingly begins with repeatability, and here the record admits only two mutually exclusive possibilities: either the incorrect result never recurred on the original machine, or it recurred when the job was re-run on that same machine; one of these must be the case, and they cannot both be.

Google engineers documented defective CPU cores producing erroneous results in a 2021 paper titled "Cores that don't count", and that documentation led directly to the practice of re-running the identical binary on a different machine, now a standard step in isolating a hardware fault. [1] That the wrong answer returned when the job was re-run on the original machine confirms that defective CPU cores fail deterministically on every repetition of the same workload. A result that never returns on the original machine, by contrast, is evidence of nondeterminism internal to the program's own execution rather than of silicon that misbehaves identically each time.

Data races in multithreaded code yield results that vary between executions of the same program. Deterministic record-and-replay tools capture nondeterministic inputs so that a failing execution can be re-executed exactly. Checksums on intermediate results localize the stage of a computation at which corruption first appears. [2] Taken together, these instruments convert an unreproducible wrong answer into a tractable object of investigation. The identical binary is exercised on a second socket and a third, so that a fault confined to one part of the fleet separates itself from one that travels with the code; the suspect execution is captured and replayed under fixed inputs, so that a defect in the program must reappear if it is there at all; and the arithmetic is audited stage by stage until the first divergence is pinned to a particular kernel or a particular device. Where replay reproduces the error with every input held constant, the weight of evidence falls on the program. Where the same binary and the same recorded inputs diverge only on one machine, and the vendor's errata or margin tests corroborate the finding, the weight falls on the part.
